headline: NP $7,410 on 20% fewer leads — Bing and the top-up did the lifting
commentary:
### The day
- **$7,410 NP at 17.6% NM**, ahead of last Monday on less spend.
  - NP: $7,410 v $6,402 last Monday
  - NM: 17.6% v 14.0%
  - Eight-Monday average NP: $5,261
- Volume was thin and so was cost; margin did the work.
  - Leads: 2,385 v 3,022 Monday average
  - Cost: $34,657 v $43,118 average Monday
  - EPL: $17.64 v $15.77 eight-Monday mean
- Month still well ahead of September, and on far less spend.
  - MTD NP: $142,781 v $129,965
  - MTD NM: 14.4% v 10.5%
  - MTD cost: $848,434 v $1,107,776
### What drove it
- Search did less with less: fewer leads, softer EPL, lower cost.
  - Search leads: 1,031 v 1,112 last Monday
  - Search EPL: $26.06 v $31.36
  - Search NP: $1,514 v $4,639
- Bing and the free lines covered that gap and then some.
  - Bing NP: $1,753 v $354
  - Bing EPL: $14.66 v $11.51
  - Remarketing plus no-source: $1,769 v $1,059
- The **RateSpecial top-up** came in heavy, which is most of the swing.
  - Top-up: $2,085 v $129 last Monday
  - Day-on-day NP gain: $1,007
- CPC came down across Search and we bought less payday_alternative.
  - Search CPC: $11.80 v $13.22
  - payday_alternative spend: $7,719 v $11,050
  - amount impression share: 24.3% v 36.4%
### Tests
| Test | Set-up | Spend 26/10 | Spend wk ago | Change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| competitor | ROAS target, no SA | $938 | $1,153 | — |
| personal | ROAS target, no SA | $177 | $270 | — |
| speed | target stepping down | $484 | $729 | — |
| competitor_scavenger | cheap-click pair | $839 | $596 | — |
| generic_scavenger | cheap-click pair | $194 | $241 | — |
- Scavengers switch back on after the weekend pause, hunting the cheap clicks.
  - competitor_scavenger CPC: $3.40 v $11.80 Search
- speed stays small by design while its target walks back down.
  - speed clicks: 30 v 41 last Monday
watch: Search EPL at $26.06 sits under the $28.58 month-to-date figure, so we're tracking where the week settles.
The 12-point drop in amount's impression share, against spend that actually went up — we're watching whether clicks hold.
Whether the $2,085 RateSpecial top-up is a one-off catch-up or closer to a new run rate.
